ci: benchmark history on GitHub Pages, 2% regression alerts (#194)

* ci: benchmark history on GitHub Pages, 2% regression alerts

- test/embedded/bench_report.h: benchReport() prints one machine-readable
  line per result, BENCH|<name>|<value>|<unit>; the datalog, mult_asm and
  fastdivision benchmarks report their 19 results so (cycles, or us for
  the micros() based ones). simavr is cycle-accurate: the values are the
  same from run to run (checked), only code changes move them.
- scripts/ci/bench_to_json.py: these lines as JSON for
  benchmark-action/github-action-benchmark (customSmallerIsBetter); fails
  on no result or a name reported twice.
- build.yml: the embedded tests run verbose and upload their results
  (also shown in the job summary); every build uploads its flash and RAM.
  A new benchmarks job, the only writer to gh-pages: a push to dev adds a
  point to the history (gh-pages/bench, charts at /bench/); a pull
  request is compared with the last point, and anything more than 2%
  worse gets a comment (not from forks, read-only token). No failure.
- doxygen-gh-pages.yml: the steps of DenverCoder1's action written out,
  since its deploy cleans every file it did not generate; clean-exclude
  keeps bench/. Both jobs share the gh-pages concurrency group.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(ci): the size benchmark reuses the gh-pages branch of the speed one

The Speed step commits its result on the local gh-pages branch (pushed on
dev only); the Firmware size step then fetched gh-pages:gh-pages again,
which git rejects as non-fast-forward. skip-fetch-gh-pages: the branch is
already up to date (on dev, the Speed step has just pushed it, and the
gh-pages concurrency group keeps other writers out).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

ci: performance and size report on every pull request (#195)

* ci: performance and size report on every pull request

As ESPHome does for memory: one comment per pull request, updated at
each push, comparing the target branch with the PR (merged into it, as
CI builds it):

- baseline job: checks out the target branch at base.sha next to the PR,
  and measures it with the PR's scripts/ci/measure.sh (the target may
  predate it): the builds of the build matrix, and the BENCH| results of
  the embedded tests;
- pr-report job: scripts/ci/pr_report.py compares these figures with the
  PR's (the artifacts of the build and test-embedded jobs): flash and RAM
  of every build, the changed benchmarks (all of them folded), ESPHome's
  marks (📈 🚨 beyond 2% worse, 📈 🔸 below, 📉 ✅ / 🎉 better), new and
  removed results. Job summary always; the comment, found by its hidden
  marker and edited in place, unless the PR comes from a fork. A failed
  baseline still gives a report, with the PR's figures alone.
- the history job (gh-pages) now runs on pushes to dev only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(build): branch and commit in the firmware on Linux too

inject_sketch_name.py called git with shell=True and a list of
arguments: on Linux, that only runs the first element, a bare 'git',
which fails - Linux builds (CI included) always said N/A for the branch
and the commit. git now runs without a shell, in the project directory,
and any failure or empty output gives N/A (no git, not a repository,
detached HEAD as in CI checkouts). The hash has a fixed length
(--short=8), so that the firmware size does not move with it: the PR
report compares sizes to the byte.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(ci): measure.sh keeps pio's output out of the JSON

On a fresh runner, pio prints its package installs on stdout, which
measure() pipes into jq: the baseline failed with a jq parse error.
pio's output now goes to stderr.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

ci: GitHub Pages landing page, firmware size history on two charts (#196)

- pages/index.html: a landing page linking the code documentation, the size
  history, the repository, and the user documentation and configurator.
- pages/bench/index.html: flash and RAM, one chart each, every build
  configuration on it, to compare configurations and follow them over time.
  End-of-line labels, tooltips with the commit, a table view, light and dark.
- scripts/ci/pages_update.py: publishes the pages and appends the sizes to
  bench/history.json, seeded from the former github-action-benchmark data.
- build.yml: the benchmarks job becomes the pages job, without
  github-action-benchmark; the speed history is dropped (the functions
  benchmarked rarely change), the PR report keeps the speed figures.
- doxygen-gh-pages.yml: deploys to doc/.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs: firmware history for September to November 2026 (#197)

The history in the main page of the doc stopped in January 2026. Each
month from the merged pull requests of dev; February to August only had
dependency bumps and personal branches.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
